generøs.explanation: "Generøs" means "generous". To say what someone is generous with, put "med" (with) after it: "Hun er generøs med sin tid" (She is generous with her time). The opposite is "nærig" (stingy): "Han er nærig" (He is stingy).

generøsitet.explanation: "En generøsitet" means "generosity". It comes from "generøs" (generous). To thank someone for giving, say: "Vi takker for din generøsitet" (We thank you for your generosity).

genetik.explanation: "Genetik" means "genetics". It comes from "et gen" (a gene). To say a trait is in the genes, say: "Det ligger i genetikken" (It is in the genetics).

genetisk.explanation: "Genetisk" means "genetic". It comes from "genetik" (genetics). To say a trait comes from the parents, say: "Hans øjenfarve er genetisk" (His eye color is genetic).

genial.explanation: "Genial" means "brilliant". It comes from "et geni" (a genius). To praise a person, say: "Hun er genial" (She is brilliant).

gennem.explanation: "Gennem" means "through". When you talk about time, it means "throughout": "Jeg har boet her gennem mange år" (I have lived here for many years).

gennemført.explanation: "Gennemført" means "polished". It comes from "at gennemføre" (to carry out). It also means "carried out", as in "Planen blev gennemført" (The plan was carried out).

gennemsigtig.explanation: "Gennemsigtig" means "transparent". It is built from "gennem" (through) and "sigt" (sight). To describe a process that hides nothing, say: "en gennemsigtig proces" (a transparent process).

gennemsnitlig.explanation: "Gennemsnitlig" means "average". It comes from "et gennemsnit" (an average). To say a day was ordinary, use "almindelig" (ordinary) instead: "Det var en almindelig dag" (It was an ordinary day).

genoptræning.explanation: "Genoptræning" means "rehabilitation". It is built from "gen-" (again) and "træning" (training). The part "gen-" also appears in "at gentage" (to repeat): "Kan du gentage det?" (Can you repeat that?)

gensidighed.explanation: "Gensidighed" means "mutuality". It comes from "gensidig" (mutual). To say a friendship goes both ways, say: "Der er gensidighed i vores venskab" (There is mutuality in our friendship).

geografi.explanation: "Geografi" means "geography". Spell it with "f", not "ph" as in English: "geografi".

gerne.explanation: "Gerne" means "gladly". To ask politely, add it to "vil have". Without it, "Jeg vil have en øl" (I want a beer) sounds blunt. To say you are glad to help, say: "Jeg hjælper dig gerne" (I am glad to help you).

gerrig.explanation: "Gerrig" means "stingy". To praise someone who is careful with money, use "sparsommelig" (thrifty) instead: "Hun er sparsommelig" (She is thrifty).

gerrighed.explanation: "En gerrighed" means "stinginess". It comes from "gerrig" (stingy). To name being careful with money in a good way, use "sparsommelighed" (thrift): "Sparsommelighed er en dyd" (Thrift is a virtue).

gift.explanation: "Gift" means "married". To name the partner, add "med" (with) after "gift". To say people got married, use "blive gift" (to get married): "De blev gift i 2015" (They got married in 2015). The same spelling is also the word for "poison": "Slangen har gift" (The snake has poison).

gin.explanation: "Gin" means "gin". To talk about the drink in general, leave out "en": "Jeg kan ikke lide gin" (I do not like gin). To talk about one serving, use "en": "Hun drikker en gin" (She is drinking a gin).

glad.explanation: "Glad" means "happy". To name the thing that makes you happy, add "for" (about) after "glad": "Jeg er glad for gaven" (I am happy about the gift).

glad for.explanation: "Glad for" means "fond of". With a thing, it means "happy with": "Hun er glad for sin bil" (She is happy with her car). To say you love someone, use "elske" (to love) instead: "Jeg elsker dig" (I love you).

glat.explanation: "Glat" means "smooth". The same word means "slippery": "Isen er glat" (The ice is slippery).

glimrende.explanation: "Glimrende" means "excellent". It comes from "at glimre" (to shine). To say things are going excellently, say: "Det går glimrende" (It is going excellently).

global.explanation: "Global" means "global". It comes from "en globus" (a globe). The opposite is "lokal" (local): "en lokal avis" (a local newspaper).

global opvarmning.explanation: "Global opvarmning" means "global warming". "Opvarmning" comes from "at varme op" (to warm up), where "op" means "up": "Jeg varmer maden op" (I warm up the food).

gluten.explanation: "Gluten" means "gluten". To say a food has none, add "-fri" (free): "Brødet er glutenfrit" (The bread is gluten-free).

glutenfri.explanation: "Glutenfri" means "gluten-free". It is built from "gluten" and "fri" (free). The part "fri" also appears in "alkoholfri" (alcohol-free): "alkoholfri øl" (alcohol-free beer).
